title: Fault Escaping: Improving Robustness of DPU Enhanced Platform with Mutual Assisted VM Recovery
problem: Modern cloud servers that use DPUs to offload virtualization split VM state across the DPU SoC and the host, so a failure in either component crashes the entire machine and all hosted VMs, with no fault-tolerant mechanism designed for this split-hypervisor architecture.
method: The paper proposes fault escaping: a scheme that treats the split hypervisors on the DPU SoC and the host as redundant peers. Using hybrid synchronization, the full VM state (in a verified, consistent snapshot) is kept accessible on either the DPU or the host with minimal synchronization overhead (kilobytes of data). When one side fails, VMs migrate their state to the surviving peer and resume execution there, bypassing the failed component rather than attempting to recover it. The hybrid synchronization protocol differentiates hot and cold VM state to minimize cross-component bandwidth.

title: Fast Linear Solvers via AI-Tuned Markov Chain Monte Carlo-based Matrix Inversion
problem: Solving large sparse linear systems is pervasive in science/engineering; Krylov solvers can be slow for ill-conditioned matrices; MCMC-based preconditioners effective but parameter selection is manual/grid-search (costly)
method: AI-driven framework using graph neural network surrogate to predict preconditioning speed; Bayesian acquisition function selects parameter sets minimizing iterations; applied to ill-conditioned linear systems

title: Scalable Neural Network Training: Distributed Data-Parallel Approaches
problem: Optimizing communication performance in hierarchical multi-GPU systems

title: Open Composer: A Web-Based Application for Generating and Managing Batch Jobs on HPC Clusters
problem: Submitting batch jobs on HPC clusters requires familiarity with Linux commands and job schedulers, creating a significant learning barrier for beginners and reducing HPC accessibility
method: Web-based application built on Open OnDemand platform providing form-driven shell script generation, real-time preview, direct script editing, job submission, and status monitoring with reusable parameters

title: PiSPICE: Accelerating Post-Layout SPICE Simulation via Essential Parasitic Identification
problem: Post-layout SPICE simulation of advanced-node ICs involves billions to trillions of parasitic nodes, creating prohibitively high computational cost that slows design closure and verification cycles.
method: PiSPICE uses adjoint sensitivity analysis on pre-layout circuits to identify critical parasitic elements and eliminate non-critical ones. Only critical parasitics are retained in post-layout simulation; model order reduction minimizes their impact while non-critical parasitics are pruned entirely, dramatically reducing simulation scale.

title: PyraNet: A Multi-Layered Hierarchical Dataset for Verilog
problem: LLMs struggle to generate high-quality Verilog code due to lack of well-organized, high-quality training datasets and specialized fine-tuning methods tailored to hardware description languages.
method: Introduces PyraNet, an open-source hierarchical multi-layered dataset for Verilog, combined with a specialized fine-tuning technique leveraging the dataset's hierarchical structure. The approach enables LLMs to generate syntactically and functionally correct Verilog through improved training data organization.

title: Leveraging Critical Proof Obligations for Efficient IC3 Verification
problem: IC3 model-checking methods spend significant effort tracking proof obligations (states to prove unreachable), creating a bottleneck in hardware verification performance due to inefficient proof obligation management.
method: Introduces Critical Proof Obligations (CPOs) that identify high-impact proof obligations, and applies two techniques: CPO-Driven UNSAT Core Generation to extract minimal sets of constraints, and CPO-Driven Proof Obligation Propagation to accelerate frame refinement and lemma discovery.

title: PHOENIX: Pauli-Based High-Level Optimization Engine for Instruction Execution on NISQ Devices
problem: Variational quantum algorithms require compilation at gate level, missing high-level Pauli-based optimization opportunities for Hamiltonian simulation programs.
method: PHOENIX operates on Pauli-based IR using binary symplectic form (BSF) to formally describe Pauli strings. It reformulates IR synthesis as BSF column-weight reduction via Clifford transformations, with heuristic simplification searching for optimal 2Q operators and TETRIS-like global ordering.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper ThirstyFLOPS: Water Footprint Modeling and Analysis Toward Sustainable HPC Systems
problem: Evaluating sustainability metrics and water footprint models for HPC systems requires independent reproducibility assessment.
method: Artifact evaluation of ThirstyFLOPS paper examining water usage modeling for HPC systems. Assessment conducted by SC25 Reproducibility Committee.

title: Basilisk: A 34mm² End-to-End Open-Source 64-bit Linux-Capable RISC-V SoC in 130nm BiCMOS
problem: End-to-end open-source EDA flows have not demonstrated large, production-grade SoCs; existing approaches scale only to small designs, limiting adoption and supply-chain independence.
method: Basilisk uses open-source EDA (Yosys synthesis, OpenROAD place-and-route) to design a 34mm² Linux-capable RISC-V SoC in 130nm BiCMOS. The team enhanced the EDA flow: 2.3x timing improvement and 1.6x area reduction in synthesis, 12% die-size reduction in P&R through technology-aware tuning. The design includes a 64-bit core, 124MB/s DRAM controller, USB 1.1, video output, and 62Mb/s chip-to-chip link.

title: MOSS: Multi-Modal Representation Learning on Sequential Circuits
problem: Circuit representation learning faces tradeoffs: LLMs understand RTL functionality but struggle with low-level netlist behavior; GNNs model netlists but fail on large sequential circuits due to long-range dependencies.
method: MOSS fuses GNNs with LLMs: enhances D-type flip-flop (DFF) node features using fine-tuned LLM embeddings from RTL; GNN operates on reduced anchor points reducing long-range dependency burden; LLM provides global circuit embeddings for supervision; adaptive aggregation and two-phase propagation for signal modeling.

title: InstAttention: In-Storage Attention Offloading for Cost-Effective Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Long-context LLM inference at large batch sizes generates KV caches that exceed GPU VRAM capacity; offloading KV caches to SSDs via PCIe creates a critical bandwidth bottleneck that severely limits throughput.
method: InstAttention offloads both the attention computation and KV cache storage to Computational Storage Drives (CSDs), which have high internal NAND bandwidth not limited by PCIe. A flash-aware in-storage attention engine executes the attention decode phase directly inside the CSD, with KV cache management mechanisms tailored to flash access patterns (e.g., large sequential reads). Optimized P2P transmission between GPU and CSDs eliminates unnecessary data migration back across PCIe. The system targets offline inference of a 13B model on an NVIDIA A6000 GPU.

title: To Tackle Cost-Skew Tradeoff: An Adaptive Learning Approach for Hub Node Selection
problem: Clock tree skew is a critical performance limiter in chip design; achieving good balance between total wire-length cost and skew requires selecting optimal hub nodes, but this combinatorial optimization is hard to solve optimally at large scale.
method: Proposes reinforcement learning-based method for hub node selection with adaptive learning strategy. The RL agent learns to select hub nodes that optimize the cost-skew tradeoff by sampling the design space and adapting selection strategy based on feedback.

title: Zero-Value Code Specialization via Profile-Guided Control Data Flow Analysis
problem: Zero-value propagation in programs causes redundant operations that severely impact performance. Since zero-values are generated dynamically at runtime, static analysis alone cannot eliminate these redundancies.
method: ZeroSpec: A profile-guided code optimizer that combines static control data flow analysis to identify zero-value propagation patterns with runtime profiling. Uses a fine-grained cost model to evaluate optimization potential and construct targeted fast paths.

title: SDR-RDMA: Software-Defined Reliability Architecture for Planetary Scale RDMA Communication
problem: RDMA reliability layer design is complicated by millisecond-scale long-haul latencies; Selective Repeat inefficient for some link conditions
method: SDR-RDMA software-defined reliability stack with receive buffer bitmap; DPA offload for line-rate performance; extensible reliability schemes

title: A Peak Performance Model for All-to-all on Hierarchical Systems and Its Applications
problem: Optimizing communication performance in hierarchical multi-GPU systems
method: Analytical performance model for hierarchical all-to-all communication
